punchline: Kodak employed over 145,000 people; Instagram, built on digital photos, had 15.
thirty_sec: Brynjolfsson and McAfee compare Kodak, which employed over 145,000 people, with Instagram, which had 15. Digital goods can be copied at close to no cost, so a tiny team can serve a huge audience. They call the growing variety of cheap goods bounty and the growing gaps in income and wealth spread, and they say GDP misses much of the first.
